paper_id: Tang et al. - 2010 - DAWN Energy efficient data aggregation in WSN with mobile sinks
title: DAWN: Energy Efficient Data Aggregation in WSN with Mobile Sinks
motivation: Sensor batteries in large forests are hard to replace; mobile sinks can help but existing theoretical models ignore constrained paths and moving speeds.
problem_framing: Joint flow routing and mobile sink location optimization under constrained road networks and energy budgets, maximizing network lifetime.
key_insight: Decouple problem into static-to-static-sink aggregation (LP) and mobile sink tour planning (Chinese Postman variants), with virtual nodes bridging subregions.
method_signature: MLDA integer program + tree extraction + interference-free scheduling + MM k-CPP approximation for mobile sink patrol.
evaluation_criteria: Network lifetime (timeslots until first node dies) and delivery delay, validated on GreenOrbs 120-node forest testbed.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Prior work ignores moving speed of sinks, but real speeds have significant impact on energy dissipation and cannot be simply ignored.
evidence_for_taste: theoretical model of this problem remains difficult
most of existing solutions either remain heuristic at best
approximation ratio... regarding to the life time
